decisions.decision: Two steps: Cliente → Cotización, not a single screen with a customer gate
decisions.why: A quote cannot be opened without an explicit customer (the server defaults it to Público en General), and a customer-as-gate on one screen is the pattern 039 is replacing
decisions.rejected: One step with the customer as a CustomerBar gate, matching todays OrderScreen

decisions.decision: Converting a quote lands the user in the back-office order workspace on the Venta (goods) step
decisions.why: The converted order arrives with no fulfilment intent and no warehouse on any line, so it is not finishable as it stands
decisions.rejected: Landing on a read-only order detail, or staying on the quote with a link

decisions.decision: Quote line prices stay read-only; absolute price_adjustment is deferred, not dropped
decisions.why: Conversion folds price_adjustment into price anyway, so anything expressible as a markup is expressible as a discount; adopting it would diverge the quote host from the other two capture hosts for no v1 gain
decisions.rejected: An editable price / showPriceAdjustment flag on the shared line row

decisions.decision: The quotes list shows all quotes in the facility by default, not only the current users
decisions.why: Matches how the orders list behaves today and suits a back office where quoting is a shared activity
decisions.rejected: Defaulting to the API mine filter, as legacy did

decisions.decision: REVERSED 2026-09-20 — the quote is ONE step, with the customer named inside it
decisions.why: Spec 039 shipped and was then directly corrected to remove its own Cliente step; the shipped CaptureStep carries the gate itself via excludeGenericCustomer (opens the customer band searching, withholds product capture until a real customer exists). This restores the original feature description, which said capture would be the only step.
decisions.rejected: Two steps (Cliente → Cotización), the 2026-09-12 decision, now superseded

decisions.decision: A quote is carried by the existing Sale/SaleLine entities, widened — not a separate Quote entity
decisions.why: The seam forecloses it: SaleEditor.ensureOpen() returns Future<Sale> and every shared capture widget takes Sale, so a quote controller state MUST be Sale?. A separate entity buys nothing without forking the widgets or adding a sentinel-filled projection.
decisions.rejected: A separate Quote/QuoteLine entity pair; and filling order-only fields with sentinels

decisions.decision: Sale.balance becomes nullable, costing 10 edits in the POS payment surface, mitigated by one balanceOrZero getter
decisions.why: Keeping it required and passing total or 0 would make a quote LOOK payable to the one code path that must never accept one. Nullability turns that from a silent behaviour into a compile error — the right trade in the highest-consequence files in the app.
decisions.rejected: balance = total (defensible but silently payable); balance = 0 (also asserts settled)

decisions.decision: One new CaptureStep parameter, showWarehouse, gates three things together: the picker, the stock-cache seed, and the point-of-sale lookup
decisions.why: They are one decision, not three symptoms. The picker currently WRITES updateLine(warehouse:), and :189-192 resolves a default warehouse via the signed-in users register — wrong twice for a quote.
decisions.rejected: A stockAware tri-state enum; passing enabled:false (still renders a dead control and reserves 168px); letting the quote repository silently drop the field

concerns.note: Hard dependency on 039-back-office-order-workspace: the shared capture step is host-agnostic only after 039, and conversion lands in the workspace 039 creates. Both features edit the same capture files, so parallel branches will conflict.
mbe-api#213 degrades the list story: quote rows carry no customer name and list search silently ignores non-numeric terms. Does not block P1.
mbe-api#209 does not account for orders raised by quote conversion; raised upstream. Affects only whether a converted order is distinguishable from a register sale on a list row.

RESOLVED: 039 has landed; mbe-api#213 and #209 both shipped. convert_to_order stamps origin=BACK_OFFICE, so a converted order appears in Pedidos (exclusive filter) and not the POS list (inclusive filter) per spec 041.

TRAP for planning: the shipped CaptureStep takes four more params than contracts/shared-step-seam.md documents (excludeGenericCustomer, attachFulfillmentIntent, headerExtra, secondaryAction) and continueLabel is optional, not required. Build against the code, not that contract file.

HIGHEST-RISK OMISSION: the quote repository must carry its own 422 mapper. mapDioException reads 422 detail only as a list, so a plain-string detail yields validation([]) and the server message is DESTROYED. convert creates an order and mbe-api credit-checks on creation, so this path is live — and FR-030 (no point of sale) arrives this way. Fails silently, only against a live server.
039/contracts/shared-step-seam.md is STALE: documents a 4-param CaptureStep; the shipped widget takes 8 and continueLabel is optional. Tasks must be written against the code, not that file.
Two release checks the client cannot assert (quickstart): the quote list is facility-scoped server-side (endpoint has no facility param), and the live shape of converts refusal bodies.

During task generation, found 3 permission gates the plan/contracts had not made explicit: confirm (T039), cancel (T052) and duplicate (T058) each needed an access.can(salesQuotes, update|create) gate on the quote_screen.dart action, not just document-state gating. Added to tasks rather than left implicit.

expectations: Payment and delivery on the quote itself
Printing, PDF and email of a quote — no server-side rendering exists, and the sibling printing effort does not currently scope quotes
Absolute per-line price adjustment (deferred, not dropped)
Profit-margin and credit checks on quotes
Changing the orders list to show that an order came from a quote
